correctness.rationale: The exact axial support-Jacobian formula is expanded with boundary terms and parity tracked explicitly. The periodic curvature equation is mean-zero and admits uniformly convergent differentiated Fourier expansions after n^2 rescaling. The limiting square-wave primitive has mean-square derivative π²/48; weighted periodic homogenization gives π²/24, and the volume identity contributes π/2, hence π³/48. The analytic argument covers every odd n→infinity and the disk/spherical volume normalization. A separate disk-intersection volume quadrature independently agrees with support integral for five odd n to <10⁻⁹; this numeric test is not treated as proof.

originality.rationale: Full open-access Hynd paper provides extremality but not the regular-n volume asymptotic. The accessible comparison records address planar Reuleaux functionals or smooth single-harmonic axial constant-width bodies. Genuine source and semantic searches under exact coefficient, alternative revolution/volume/constant-width names found no implication of the sharp π³/48 law. This is best-knowledge originality, not a proof of global priority; classical body-of-revolution volume tables are residual risk.
residual_risks: Old geometric literature may contain exact volumes of individual Reuleaux solids of revolution or an equivalent asymptotic in different terms.
Several thematically similar published-finding corpus records were available only as titles and summaries; none was misrepresented as fully inspected.
A published generic axisymmetric support formula could simplify the proof; that does not by itself imply the family-specific asymptotic but may reduce novelty.

value.rationale: The explicit all-odd-order sequence of Hynd extreme 3D constant-width bodies converges to the unique volume-maximizing ball. Determining its exact volume-deficit scale and coefficient quantifies a nontrivial extremal/geometric tension: extremality does not imply positive separation from the ball, yet the canonical regular polygon approach has a sharp order and coefficient. This natural, invariant shape statistic is motivated independently of its calculation and differs from established planar Reuleaux area/inertia formulae.
